+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '8e80'
+title: ProcessInstallRunnerTests.cancellationTerminatesTheChildPromptly fails under full-suite load
+---
+## Problem
+In a full `swift test` run on 2026-10-17 (911 tests), `ProcessInstallRunnerTests.cancellationTerminatesTheChildPromptly()` failed: `elapsed < .seconds(5)` was false, `elapsed` was 6.17 seconds. In the same window, many tests of other suites reported "passed after 47 seconds", thus the test process did not get CPU time for a long period. The same test passed in 0.110 seconds when it ran alone (`swift test --filter "ProcessInstallRunnerTests|ChildStandardInputTests"`).
+
+The test measures real time from `task.cancel()` to `task.value`. Under load, the time includes the time that the cooperative pool and the dedicated drain thread wait for the CPU. The fixed limit of 5 seconds is a real-time assertion, thus the test can fail when the machine is busy.
+
+Found during ^w29j74j. The change of ^w29j74j (stdin of each child is the null device) does not touch the cancellation path.
+
+## Change
+- Make the assertion independent of the scheduler. For example, assert that the child is killed (the pid is gone, or the run ends with a kill signal) and that the run does not wait for `sleep 60` to end on its own, with a limit that is far below 60 seconds but far above the scheduler delay.
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+- [ ] The test proves that cancellation kills the child, not that the scheduler is fast.
+- [ ] The full unit suite passes.
+
+#test-flake
\ No newline at end of file

@@ -10,6 +10,15 @@
   id: 01m57n8swapnmy0tcx783yweew
   text: 'Research: the test is in Tests/FoundationModelsCodeContextTests/ServerInstallerTests.swift (struct ProcessInstallRunnerTests). On cancel, ProcessInstallRunner.awaitCompletion sends SIGKILL to the pid, and the terminationHandler resolves the run with exitCode = terminationStatus (the signal number, 9). The run does not throw on cancel. The child is `/usr/bin/env <tool>`; env execs the tool, thus the pid of the Process is the pid of the tool. The unit target already depends on ScriptedLSPServerSupport, thus `processExists(_:)` is available. The run does not give the pid to the caller, thus the test lets the child (`sh`) write `$$` to a file and then `exec sleep`. No other test in ProcessInstallRunnerTests or ServerInstallerTests has a real-time elapsed assertion. LspSupervisorTests has one (`elapsed < .seconds(5)` after a gated install); it is out of the scope of this card.'
   timestamp: 2026-10-18T14:04:54.026815+00:00
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m57nfafht6m7wqzxxa56vmhs
+  text: |-
+    Implementation: in ServerInstallerTests.swift, `cancellationTerminatesTheChildPromptly` is replaced by `cancellationKillsAndReapsTheChildBeforeItsSleepEnds`. The child is `sh -c 'echo $$ > "$1"; exec sleep "$2"'`. The test waits (no real-time limit, only the `.timeLimit` trait) until the pid file holds a complete line, cancels the task, and asserts: exitCode == SIGKILL, `processExists(pid)` is false (shared helper of ScriptedLSPServerSupport), and elapsed < `cancelledRunLimit` (30 s, far below the 60 s sleep, far above the scheduler delay). The other ProcessInstallRunnerTests now use named constants (`selfEndingRunTimeout`, `elapsingRunTimeout`, `childSleepSeconds`) in place of call-argument literals. No production change.
+
+    Proof that the test can fail: with the `kill(pid, SIGKILL)` of `onCancel` removed for one run, the test failed: exitCode was 0 and the run waited 60.01 s. The kill was then put back (git diff of Sources is empty).
+
+    New work: ^94wns6b for the `elapsed < .seconds(5)` assertion in LspSupervisorTests (out of the scope of this card).
